title: Barthadenovirus Coverage Audit
h1: Does the Barthadenovirus (formerly Atadenovirus) module work?
standfirst: Barthadenoviruses add two lineage-specific gene families, RH and LH, to the conserved core. The module calls the core in every near-complete genome and splits the RH family into positional orthogroups; the short unspliced 22K product was added after the panel run (16 Nov 2026).
headline_tiles: fewer distinct strings at equal depth

sections.title: What the module covers
sections.lede: Barthadenoviruses of ruminants, reptiles, birds and marsupials, with their lineage-specific RH and LH gene families.

blocks.html: 33K is called after 100K. 22K in this genus is a short (59–66 aa) unspliced read-on of 33K’s first exon; it was added after this map was drawn and is called at 20,944–21,144 in this genome (section 07). The RH genes at the right end are the positional orthogroups.

Genomes were assigned to modules from sequence alone: the genus by best hexon match, and one-fiber versus multi-fiber mastadenoviruses by a census of intact fiber genes classed by literature orthology (Podgorski 2023, PMID 36610683). Deposited names were never used to assign a genome.

sections.title: How it was built
sections.lede: Membership by homology to curated seed collections; the deposited name is recorded but never decides.

rows: 524 unique proteins assigned (≥80% coverage both ways, best feature ≥1.2× the runner-up)
173 no hit, 12 ambiguous, 50 low coverage, 1 submitter-marked partial

blocks.html: Paralogue families were split into orthogroup features by genome position, and each is called by sequence, never by location. Features with no literature function are named “Uncharacterized lineage-specific protein”. Splice junctions come from the literature and were extended to other lineages by aligning donor and acceptor sites; every spliced product was translated and checked in frame.
Self-recall (each feature’s profiles searched against its own collection) is 100% for nearly every feature; the registry page lists every feature.

sections.title: Where the cutoffs sit
sections.lede: Cutoffs left at the default are not listed; every one below was set from a measurement.

blocks.html: Every CDS scans to its stop codon (downstream_ext 1); mature peptides set both extension flags from their own termini. In the 916-genome check, every unspliced CDS call ends on a stop codon except calls that stop at an N gap or an IUPAC base in the assembly.

sections.title: Does it route?
sections.lede: A genome no rep contig claims is never annotated at all.

blocks.html: All genomes assigned to this module route to it.

sections.title: Does it call the proteins?
sections.lede: Calls per near-complete routed genome, full panel (69 genomes).

blocks.html: Lowest essential feature: 98.6%. Every essential feature is called in at least 85% of near-complete genomes.

sections.title: Are the calls right?
sections.lede: Duplicates, stop codons and cleavage sites, measured on every call.

blocks.text:

blocks.html: Extra calls listed as INSEPARABLE are documented multi-copy cases or single broken genomes; none is a second feature stacked on another feature’s locus. Same-frame overlaps between different features are limited to single genomes.

sections.title: What it cannot do
sections.lede: Named as prominently as what works.

headers: why tuning will not close it
rows: The short unspliced L4 product (59–66 aa, 33K’s first exon read on past the splice donor) was dropped by the build as unbuildable; rebuilt 16 Nov 2026 (8 sequences, 2 PSSMs) and now called, e.g. BAdV-4 20,944–21,144. The coverage numbers here predate it
Function in this genus not established
7 of 73 calls start on the AVP site; most start 5–8 aa past a site that is present
59% of calls end on the site (51% in the subset)
RH_A–RH_R and UNC_RHP_1–3 are positional orthogroups present in 0–36% of genomes
33K, E1A and E4ORF6/7 are called only where the genome is ≥95% identical (nt) to a curated reference transcript; e.g. 30 of 48 species C subset genomes have no 33K call
By design of the splice caller; left as is by the curator
A cleaved end lands where the tBLASTn HSP lands; nothing moves it onto the AVP motif
No setting does this: it needs an annotator step that snaps the end to the motif
get_splice_variant_features.pl supports one junction; UXP is called as the U-exon ORF only
Needs multi-junction support in the splice caller
Unspliced calls of spliced genes start off-Met
pol, pTP and IVa2 are called on the body exon
Expected for body-exon calls; the leader exons are not modelled
pVIc, mu, pVIIn, the propeptides, iTP and the 52K products
11–19 aa peptides are too short for a profile

sections.title: What the run found
sections.lede: Genome quality from the GTO pipeline on the 916-genome subset, with the essential genes set by the curator’s rules.

blocks.html: Essential genes (copy_num) follow the curator’s rules: never on uncharacterized proteins, special features or lineage-specific genes, and excluded wherever a cutoff, copy-number or coverage problem is on record. Essential here: DBP, E4_3, HEXON, IVA2, K100, K52, PENTON, PIIIA, POL, PROTEASE, PTP, PVI, PVII, PVIII, VI_MAT.

The subset deliberately over-samples unusual genomes, so its quality rate is a floor for the module, not an estimate of it. Poor genomes are dominated by sequence problems: deposits with no cytosine, N gaps, partial genomes and genes interrupted by stop codons.

sections.title: What the vocabulary bought
sections.lede: The point of LowVan is a controlled vocabulary. This is what it cost the free text.

items: fewer distinct strings at equal depth

blocks.html: Unbound deposits are mostly “hypothetical protein” and deposits whose sequence was ambiguous between two features; several name proteins the module does call (for example 22K and E4 ORF1 in the one-fiber mastadenoviruses), so the unbound count is not a count of missed proteins.
